mutations.description: Enhance literature grounding prompt to explicitly address technical data gaps in environmental engineering, surface science, and catalytic materials
mutations.justification: Top data gaps include 'Environmental Engineering' (criticality: high, recurrence: 2), 'Surface Science' (criticality: high), and 'Catalytic Materials' (criticality: medium). The current prompt may not sufficiently guide the agent to acknowledge and address domain-specific literature limitations. Enhanced prompt should include explicit instructions to: 1) Identify and state literature limitations for technical domains, 2) Suggest proxy literature from adjacent fields when direct literature is sparse, 3) Flag hypotheses that rely heavily on undocumented assumptions.
mutations.estimated_impact: Reduce recurrence of high-criticality data gaps by 30-50%, improve hypothesis credibility in technical domains
mutations.observation_summary: top_data_gaps: Environmental Engineering (high criticality, recurrence 2), Surface Science (high), Catalytic Materials (medium)

rationale: The observation report reveals three key opportunities: 1) Strong score-feedback correlation (0.85) indicates the scoring system is well-calibrated, but average composite scores are low (0.41) with most hypotheses in the 0.3-0.5 range. 2) Several underexplored domains show promise (Biomaterials, Ceramics, Molecular Biology). 3) Top data gaps indicate literature grounding limitations in specific technical domains. I propose targeted mutations to: increase hypothesis quality by adjusting score weights to favor testability and coherence, encourage exploration of fertile underexplored domains, and improve literature grounding for technical domains.
